'''Aihud Pevsner''' ({{Langx|he|אייהוד פבזנר}}; December 18, 1925 – June 17, 2018) was an American experimental physicist who was the lead researcher credited with the discovery of the [[Eta meson]].<ref name="jhuobit">{{cite news |title=Experimental physicist Aihud Pevsner dies at 92 |url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2018/06/21/aihud-pevsner-physicist-dies/ |accessdate=June 27, 2018 |date=June 22, 2018}}</ref>

Born in [[Haifa]], [[Mandatory Palestine]], to Yoshua Pevsner and Esther Ben-Yeshaia, Aihud Pevsner immigrated to the United States with his parents at the age of three. The family, of Belarusian-Jewish descent, settled in New York. Pevsner served in the United States Navy from 1944 to 1945, and married Lucille Wolf in 1949.

Upon earning a doctorate in physics from [[Columbia University]], he began teaching at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="jhuobit" /> In 1956, Pevsner joined the [[Johns Hopkins University]] faculty. Over the course of his career, Pevsner received two [[Guggenheim fellowships]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Aihud Pevsner |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/aihud-pevsner/ |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation |accessdate=June 27, 2018 |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513034434/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/aihud-pevsner/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> was named a [[Fulbright Scholar]], and granted fellowship by the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="jhuobit" /> He was the lead researcher credited with the discovery of the [[Eta meson]], and appointed a Jacob L. Hain professor in 1977.<ref name="jhuobit" />

Pevsner died at the age of 92 on June 17, 2018.<ref name="jhuobit" />
